questions.question: The radius of a solid cylinder is 12 cm, and its height is 25 cm. A three-dimensional sector with a sector angle of 45o is removed from it, all along the height of the cylinder. What is the volume (in cm³) of the larger piece of the cylinder?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Removed part = 45° out of 360° ⇒ removed = 1/8

Remaining volume = 7/8 of cylinder

Total volume = πr²h = π × 12² × 25 = 3600π

Required = 7/8 × 3600π = 3150π

**∴ Answer = 3150π**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 
• 
• 45° r = 12 cm 

**Given:**

r = 12 cm, h = 25 cm, angle = 45°

**Formula:**

Volume of cylinder = πr²h

Sector volume = (θ/360) × πr²h

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total volume = π × 12² × 25 = 3600π

⇒ Removed volume = (45/360) × 3600π = 1/8 × 3600π = 450π

⇒ Remaining = 3600π − 450π = 3150π

**Final Answer:** 3150π cm³

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

**Volume of Cylinder:** πr²h → depends on base area and height.

**Sector of Cylinder:** Fraction = θ/360 → same fraction applies to volume.

**Mensuration Shortcut:** Always find fraction removed first to save time.

**Angle Conversion:** 45° = 1/8 of full circle (360°).

questions.question: Which of the following is correct about Hibernation mode in computers?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Uses minimum power**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Hibernation** is a specific **power management mode** in computer operating systems that saves the current state of the system to the **Hard Disk** or **Solid State Drive (SSD)** before completely powering off.
 
• Unlike **Sleep Mode**, which keeps the system state in the **Random Access Memory (RAM)** and requires a continuous supply of electricity, **Hibernation** allows the computer to be fully turned off, meaning it **uses minimum power** (essentially zero) while preserving open documents and running applications. ***Hence, the statement regarding minimum power is correct.***
 
• When a computer enters **Hibernation**, it writes the contents of its **RAM** into a file on the storage drive, often named **hiberfil.sys** in **Windows** environments.
 
• This mode is particularly useful for **laptop** users who need to save their **battery life** for an extended period without losing their active **workspace** or closing their **programs**.
 
• The primary **function** of Hibernation is to provide a middle ground between **Sleep Mode** (fast wake-up but uses battery) and **Shut Down** (no power use but loses all open work).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Sleep Mode vs. Hibernation:**

 
 
• In **Sleep Mode**, the computer enters a low-power state, but the **RAM** remains powered to keep the data "volatile." This allows for a **near-instant wake-up** time, usually within **2 to 5 seconds**.
 
• In **Hibernation**, the wake-up time is longer (typically **20 to 40 seconds**) because the system must read the saved data back from the **Hard Drive** into the **RAM**.
 
 
 
• **Hybrid Sleep:**
 
 
• This is a combination of **Sleep** and **Hibernation** designed primarily for **desktop computers**. It saves the state to both the **RAM** and the **Hard Disk**, ensuring that if a **power failure** occurs, the data is still safe on the disk.
 
 
 
• **Storage Requirements:**
 
 
• To enable **Hibernation**, the computer must have enough **free disk space** to accommodate a file equal to the size of the installed **RAM** (e.g., if you have **8GB of RAM**, you need at least **8GB of disk space**).
 
 
 
• **Historical Context:**
 
 
• The **Hibernate** feature became widely popular with the release of **Windows 95 (OSR2)** and **Windows 98**, significantly improving **mobile computing** efficiency for early notebook users.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Power Outages:** One of the greatest **features** of Hibernation is that it protects your data against **unexpected power loss**. Since the state is stored on a **non-volatile storage medium**, even if the battery dies or the plug is pulled, your **data remains intact**.
 
• **Hardware Wear:** On older **Hard Disk Drives (HDDs)**, frequent hibernating might involve significant mechanical read/write actions, but on modern **SSDs**, this process is highly efficient, though it does contribute to the **Total Bytes Written (TBW)** metric over a **number of years**.
 
• **Modern Standby:** In newer **Windows 10** and **Windows 11** devices, a feature called **Modern Standby (S0 Low Power Idling)** is replacing traditional sleep/hibernate to allow the PC to stay **connected to the internet** and receive **notifications** while in a low-power state.
 
• **When to use:** It is recommended to use **Hibernation** if you will not be using your **laptop** for more than **2 or 3 hours**, or if you want to keep your **current state** but have no access to a **charging port**.

questions.question: The Battle of Wandiwash was fought between:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**British and French**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Battle of Wandiwash** was a decisive battle in **Indian history**, fought on **January 22, 1760**.
 
• It was a major confrontation between the **British East India Company** and the **French East India Company**.
 
• The **British** forces were led by **Sir Eyre Coote**, while the **French** forces were commanded by the **Comte de Lally**.
 
• This battle was the turning point of the **Third Carnatic War** (**1758–1763**), which was the **Indian** theater of the global **Seven Years' War** fought between **Britain** and **France**.
 
• The **British** emerged victorious, effectively ending **French** colonial ambitions in **India** and paving the way for **British** supremacy over the **Indian subcontinent**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **The Carnatic Wars:**

 
 
• These were a series of **three** military conflicts in the middle of the **18th century** on the **Indian subcontinent**.
 
• The conflicts involved numerous nominally independent rulers and their vassals, struggles for succession and territory, and included a diplomatic and military struggle between the **French East India Company** and the **British East India Company**.
 
• The wars were mainly fought in the territories of the **Nizam of Hyderabad** and the **Carnatic** region (modern-day **Tamil Nadu** and **Andhra Pradesh**).
 
 
 
• **Treaty of Paris (1763):**
 
 
• The **Seven Years' War** ended with the signing of the **Treaty of Paris** in **1763**.
 
• According to the treaty, the **French** factories (trading posts) in **India**, such as **Pondicherry** and **Chandernagore**, were restored to **France**.
 
• However, the **French** were prohibited from fortifying these settlements or maintaining large armies in **India**, which ensured **British** dominance.
 
 
 
• **Key Figures:**
 
 
• **Sir Eyre Coote:** A **British** soldier who gained fame for his role in the **Battle of Wandiwash** and later became the Commander-in-Chief of the **British** forces in **India**.
 
• **Comte de Lally:** A **French** general of **Irish** descent who was later executed in **France** for his failure in the **Indian** campaign.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Location:** The battle took place at **Wandiwash**, which is now known as **Vandavasi**, located in the **Tiruvannamalai** district of **Tamil Nadu**, **India**.
 
• **Military Strength:** The **British** army consisted of approximately **1,900 European** troops and **2,100 Indian** sepoys, while the **French** army had around **2,250 European** troops and **1,300 Indian** allies.
 
• **Consequences for Other Powers:**
 
 
• **Portuguese:** By the **18th century**, **Portuguese** influence in **India** was largely confined to **Goa**, **Daman**, and **Diu**. They were not major participants in the **Carnatic Wars**.
 
• **Dutch:** The **Dutch** power in **India** had already been significantly weakened following their defeat by the **British** in the **Battle of Chinsurah** (also known as the **Battle of Biderra**) in **1759**.
 
 
 
• **Impact on French Settlements:** Following the defeat at **Wandiwash**, the **French** capital of **Pondicherry** was besieged and fell to the **British** in **January 1761**, marking the complete collapse of **French** political power in **India**.

questions.question: After the Government merged 29 labour laws into four Labour Codes in November 2025, the provision permitting women to work in all establishments including night shifts falls under which of the following Codes?

options.text: The Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code, 2020

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code, 2020**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code, 2020** is the specific legislation that provides for the employment of women in all establishments for all types of work. This includes permitting women to work during **night shifts**, which is defined as the period between **7 PM and 6 AM**. *Hence, the statement regarding women working in night shifts falls under this code.*
 
• Under this code, the **Government** mandates that if a woman is required to work at night, the **employer** must ensure adequate **safety, health, and welfare facilities**. Furthermore, the **prior consent** of the woman worker is a mandatory requirement before assigning her to a night shift.
 
• This code is a massive reform that consolidates and replaces **13 central labour laws**, including the **Factories Act, 1948**, the **Mines Act, 1952**, and the **Contract Labour (Regulation and Abolition) Act, 1970**.
 
• The primary objective of this code is to regulate the **health and safety conditions** of workers in establishments with **10 or more workers** and in all **mines and docks**, ensuring a standardized environment across **India**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **The Code on Wages, 2019:**

 
 
• This was the **first code** to be passed by **Parliament** in **August 2019**. It replaced **four** existing laws: the **Payment of Wages Act, 1936**, the **Minimum Wages Act, 1948**, the **Payment of Bonus Act, 1965**, and the **Equal Remuneration Act, 1976**.
 
• It ensures that there is **no discrimination** on the ground of **gender** in matters relating to **wages** and recruitment for the same work or work of a similar nature.
 
 
 
• **The Industrial Relations Code, 2020:**
 
 
• This code consolidates **three** functional central labour laws: the **Trade Unions Act, 1926**, the **Industrial Employment (Standing Orders) Act, 1946**, and the **Industrial Disputes Act, 1947**.
 
• It aims to improve **business efficiency** by increasing the threshold for **retrenchment** and closure in industrial establishments from **100 to 300 workers** without requiring prior government permission.
 
 
 
• **The Code on Social Security, 2020:**
 
 
• This code replaces **nine** laws, including the **Employees’ Provident Fund Act, 1952**, and the **Maternity Benefit Act, 1961**.
 
• A significant feature of this code is the **universalization** of social security benefits, extending coverage to **unorganized workers**, **gig workers**, and **platform workers** for the first time in **India**.
 
 
 
• **Broad Labour Reform Context:**
 
 
• The **Government of India** decided to amalgamate **29 central labour laws** into **four Labour Codes** based on the recommendations of the **Second National Commission on Labour (2002)**.
 
• The goal of these reforms is to provide **ease of doing business** while ensuring **worker protection** and **transparency** through **digitalization** and simplified **compliance**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Empowerment of Women:** By allowing women to work in all sectors (including **hazardous processes** with safeguards), the **OSH Code 2020** removes traditional barriers that limited **female labor force participation**.
 
• **Annual Health Check-up:** The **OSH Code** introduces a provision for a **free annual health check-up** for workers above a certain **age** (usually **45 years**) in specific establishments, enhancing the **preventive healthcare** framework for the **workforce**.
 
• **Inter-State Migrant Workers:** The code provides specific benefits for **migrant workers**, including a **journey allowance** and the **"One Nation, One Ration Card"** facility to ensure **food security** when they move across **state boundaries** for **employment**.

questions.question: Ustad Ahmad Lahori is renowned as the chief architect of which UNESCO World Heritage Site?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Taj Mahal, Agra**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ustad Ahmad Lahori** is celebrated as the **chief architect** of the **Taj Mahal**, one of the most iconic structures of **Mughal architecture**. He was a master builder in the court of **Emperor Shah Jahan** and is often credited with the creative vision behind this **UNESCO World Heritage Site**.
 
• The **Taj Mahal** was commissioned by **Emperor Shah Jahan** in the **year 1631** to house the tomb of his favorite wife, **Mumtaz Mahal**. It also serves as the final resting place for the **Emperor** himself.
 
• Construction of the **Taj Mahal** complex is believed to have begun in **1632**. The **main mausoleum** was completed in **1648**, while the surrounding buildings and gardens were finished by **1653**.
 
• **Ahmad Lahori** is also traditionally credited as the architect of the **Red Fort** (Lal Qila) in **Delhi**, showing his significant influence on the **Golden Age** of **Mughal** building projects.
 
• The monument was designated as a **UNESCO World Heritage Site** in **1983** for being "the jewel of **Muslim art** in **India** and one of the universally admired masterpieces of the world's heritage."

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Fatehpur Sikri, Agra**:

 
 
• Founded in **1571** by **Emperor Akbar**, it served as the capital of the **Mughal Empire** until **1585**.
 
• It is famous for the **Buland Darwaza** (Gate of Magnificence), which was built to commemorate **Akbar's** victory over **Gujarat**.
 
• The architectural style is a blend of **Hindu** and **Muslim** traditions. *Hence, this option is incorrect regarding Ustad Ahmad Lahori.*
 
 
 
• **Humayun's Tomb, Delhi**:
 
 
• Commissioned by **Humayun's** first wife, **Empress Bega Begum** (also known as Haji Begum), in **1558**.
 
• The **chief architect** was **Mirak Mirza Ghiyas**, a **Persian** designer.
 
• It was the **first garden-tomb** on the **Indian subcontinent** and inspired the design of the **Taj Mahal**. *Hence, this option is incorrect.*
 
 
 
• **Jaisalmer Fort, Rajasthan**:
 
 
• Built in **1156 AD** by the **Bhati Rajput** ruler **Rawal Jaisal**.
 
• It is known as the **Sonar Quila** or **Golden Fort** because of its **yellow sandstone** walls that shimmer like gold in the sunlight.
 
• It is one of the few "living forts" in the world, as a portion of the city's population still resides inside. *Hence, this option is incorrect.*
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Architectural Features**: The **Taj Mahal** is renowned for its **perfect symmetry**, the use of **white Makrana marble**, and the **Pietra Dura** (parchin kari) inlay work using **semi-precious stones**.
 
• **The Charbagh**: The complex features a **300-meter** square **Charbagh** (Mughal garden), which uses raised pathways that divide each of the four quarters of the garden into **16** sunken flowerbeds.
 
• **Global Recognition**: In **2007**, the **Taj Mahal** was declared a winner of the **New 7 Wonders of the World** (2000–2007) initiative.
 
• **Material Sourcing**: While the marble came from **Rajasthan**, **Jasper** was sourced from **Punjab**, **Jade** and **Crystal** from **China**, **Turquoise** from **Tibet**, and **Lapis Lazuli** from **Afghanistan**.

questions.question: An object is placed between the focus and the pole of a concave mirror. The image formed is _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**virtual and upright**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• When an object is placed between the **pole (P)** and the **principal focus (F)** of a **concave mirror**, the light rays originating from the object diverge after reflection from the mirror surface.
 
• Since the reflected rays are diverging, they do not intersect in front of the mirror to form a **real image**. Instead, when these rays are produced backwards, they appear to meet at a point **behind the mirror**.
 
• The nature of the image formed in this specific case is **virtual**, meaning it cannot be projected onto a screen.
 
• The orientation of the image is **upright** (also known as **erect**), which means it is in the same vertical direction as the object.
 
• Regarding the size, the image is **magnified** or **enlarged**, being significantly larger than the actual **object**.
 
• This is the **unique position** for a **concave mirror** where it acts as a magnifying glass, producing a **virtual and upright** image instead of the usual **real and inverted** images produced at other positions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Concave Mirror (Converging Mirror):**

 
 
• A **concave mirror** is a spherical mirror with an inward-curving reflecting surface. It is often called a **converging mirror** because it tends to collect light that falls on it, refocusing parallel incoming rays to a **focus**.
 
• The **focal length (f)** of a **concave mirror** is considered **negative** according to the **Cartesian sign convention**.
 
• The relationship between the **radius of curvature (R)** and **focal length (f)** is given by the **formula** **R = 2f**.
 
 
 
• **Applications/Uses of this Property:**
 
 
• **Shaving Mirrors:** Men use **concave mirrors** to see a **magnified** and **upright** image of the face for a better shave.
 
• **Dentists' Mirrors:** Dentists use these mirrors to see **enlarged** images of the teeth of patients while keeping the mirror very close (within the **focal length**).
 
• **Makeup Mirrors:** Used to provide a clear, **upright**, and **enlarged** view of facial **features**.
 
 
 
• **Image Characteristics at Different Positions:**
 
 
• **At Infinity:** The image is formed at the **Focus (F)**; it is **real, inverted**, and **highly diminished**.
 
• **Beyond C (Center of Curvature):** The image is formed **between F and C**; it is **real, inverted**, and **diminished**.
 
• **At C:** The image is formed **at C**; it is **real, inverted**, and of the **same size** as the object.
 
• **Between C and F:** The image is formed **beyond C**; it is **real, inverted**, and **enlarged**.
 
• **At F:** The image is formed **at infinity**; it is **real, inverted**, and **highly enlarged**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Real vs Virtual Image:** A **real image** is formed when light rays actually meet at a point after reflection, whereas a **virtual image** is formed when light rays only appear to diverge from a point. **Real images** are always **inverted** in mirrors, while **virtual images** are always **upright**.
 
• **Mirror Formula:** The position of the image can be calculated using the **mirror formula**: **1/f = 1/v + 1/u**, where **v** is the **image distance**, **u** is the **object distance**, and **f** is the **focal length**.
 
• **Magnification (m):** It is the ratio of the **height of the image** to the **height of the object**. For **virtual images** in a mirror, the **magnification** value is **positive**.

questions.question: Which among the following regions saw the Bundela's uprising in 1842?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Jabalpur**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Bundela Uprising** of **1842** was a significant armed rebellion against the **British East India Company** in **Central India**.
 
• The uprising was primarily centered in the **Sagar-Narmada territories**, which encompasses regions like **Jabalpur**, **Sagar**, **Damoh**, **Narsinghpur**, and **Hoshangabad**. ***Hence, the region of Jabalpur saw the uprising in 1842.***
 
• The rebellion was led by prominent local landlords and chieftains, most notably **Madhukar Shah** of **Narhut** and **Jawahar Singh Bundela** of **Chandrapur**.
 
• The primary cause of the revolt was the **oppressive land revenue policy** and the high **tax assessments** (the **Malguari system**) imposed by the **British** after they annexed the **Saugor and Nerbudda territories** from the **Marathas** in **1818**.
 
• Other leaders like **Delan Shah**, a **Gond** chief from **Narsinghpur**, also joined the movement, making it a combined effort of **Bundela** and **Gond** tribes against **British** exploitation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Vizianagram:**

 
 
• This region is located in the modern-day state of **Andhra Pradesh**.
 
• It was the site of a revolt in **1794** when the **Raja of Vizianagram**, **Vizieram Rauze**, rose against the **British East India Company** after they attempted to disband his troops and demanded a huge tribute.
 
• This event is historically distinct from the **Bundela uprising** and occurred nearly **50 years earlier**.
 
 
 
• **Saurashtra:**
 
 
• Located in **Gujarat**, this region saw various resistances against the **British**, such as the **Vheras** uprising between **1818 and 1820**.
 
• The **Bundelas** were not geographically associated with **Saurashtra**, as their influence was concentrated in **Central India** (modern **Madhya Pradesh** and **Uttar Pradesh**).
 
 
 
• **Ganjam:**
 
 
• Located in **Odisha**, **Ganjam** was the center of multiple uprisings, including the **Ganjam Rebellion** led by **Dhananjaya Bhanja**, the **Raja of Gumsur**, in **1835-37**.
 
• Another notable movement in this region was the **Savara Rebellion** (**1853-1856**). These events were unrelated to the **Bundela** ethnic group or the **1842** timeline of the **Sagar-Narmada** territories.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Consequences:** The **British** authorities, under **Lord Ellenborough**, used military force to suppress the **Bundela Uprising**. By **1843**, the main leaders were captured or surrendered. **Madhukar Shah** was executed by the **British**, becoming a local martyr.
 
• **Geopolitical Impact:** Although the **1842** rebellion was localized, it reflected the deep-seated resentment against **British** interference in traditional land-holding systems. It is often seen by historians as a precursor to the **Great Revolt of 1857** in **Central India**.
 
• **Administrative Changes:** Following the unrest, the **British** were forced to make some administrative adjustments to the revenue collection system in the **Sagar-Narmada** territories to prevent further mass dissatisfaction.
 
• **Role of Forest Tribes:** The **1842** movement was unique because it bridged the gap between the **Bundela** ruling class and the tribal **Gonds**, demonstrating a unified front against **colonial** rule in the **Vindhyan** and **Satpura** ranges.

questions.question: What trend is noted in the share of agriculture in GDP from 1950–51 to 2016–17?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Significant reduction**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The share of **agriculture and allied sectors** in India’s **Gross Domestic Product (GDP)** has witnessed a **Significant reduction** over the decades, dropping from approximately **51.8%** in **1950-51** to about **15.4%** to **17.4%** by **2016-17**. This reflects the structural transformation of the Indian economy from agrarian to service-oriented.
 
• In the early years of independence (**1950s**), agriculture was the backbone of the economy, providing the majority of national income and employment. However, as the **Industrial (Secondary)** and **Service (Tertiary)** sectors grew at much higher rates, the relative contribution of agriculture naturally declined.
 
• The trend of **Significant reduction** does not imply a decrease in total agricultural production; in fact, India’s food grain production increased from about **50 million tonnes** in **1950** to over **275 million tonnes** by **2016-17**. The decline is strictly in terms of its percentage share in the overall **GDP**.
 
• During the **Planning Era**, especially after the **Second Five-Year Plan**, the focus shifted toward **heavy industries**, and later, after the **1991 Liberalization**, toward the **Service Sector**, which accelerated the shrinking share of the primary sector.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Sectoral Composition of GDP:**

 
 
• The **Primary Sector** (Agriculture, Mining, Fishing) share has decreased consistently.
 
• The **Secondary Sector** (Manufacturing, Electricity, Construction) saw moderate growth but has remained relatively stagnant compared to services.
 
• The **Tertiary Sector** (Services, Trade, Transport, Communication) has seen an explosive rise, contributing more than **53%** of the **GDP** in **2016-17**.
 
 
 
• **Employment vs. GDP Contribution:**
 
 
• There is a major disparity in India where agriculture contributes only about **15-17%** to **GDP** but still employs nearly **43-49%** of the total **workforce** as of **2016**.
 
• This phenomenon is often termed **"disguised unemployment,"** where more people are engaged in agriculture than are actually required for the current level of production.
 
 
 
• **The Green Revolution (1960s):**
 
 
• The introduction of **High Yielding Variety (HYV) seeds**, better irrigation, and fertilizers under the leadership of **M.S. Swaminathan** significantly boosted productivity but did not stop the declining trend of agriculture’s share in **GDP** relative to other booming sectors.
 
 
 
• **Economic Liberalization 1991:**
 
 
• The **LPG (Liberalization, Privatization, and Globalization)** reforms opened the economy, leading to a surge in **Information Technology (IT)** and **Banking**, which further overshadowed the agricultural contribution.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Gross Value Added (GVA):** Recent economic data uses **GVA** at basic prices to measure sectoral performance. In **2016-17**, the **GVA** growth for agriculture was around **6.3%**, though its total share remained low.
 
• **Data Collection:** The **Central Statistics Office (CSO)**, under the **Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI)**, is the nodal agency responsible for calculating these **GDP** figures and sectoral shares.
 
• **Engel’s Law:** This economic principle suggests that as family income rises, the proportion of income spent on food declines, even if absolute expenditure on food rises. This contributes to the long-term decline of the agricultural sector’s share in a developing economy’s **GDP**.

questions.question: Which of the following ports have NOT been identified for Port Modernization and Maritime Infrastructure Expansion under the Maritime Amrit Kaal Vision 2047 (MAKV 2047)?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Panaji Port**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Maritime Amrit Kaal Vision 2047 (MAKV 2047)** is a comprehensive roadmap launched by Prime Minister **Narendra Modi** in **October 2023** during the **Global Maritime India Summit** to transform India's maritime sector over the next **25 years**.
 
• The vision identifies several **Major Port Authorities** for massive modernization and infrastructure expansion to create "Mega Ports" with a capacity exceeding **300 to 500 MTPA**. **Deendayal Port Authority (Kandla)** in **Gujarat** is a primary site identified for such expansion due to its strategic location and existing high cargo throughput. ***Hence, the statement regarding Deendayal Port is correct as it is identified for expansion.***
 
• **V.O. Chidambaranar Port Authority (Tuticorin)** in **Tamil Nadu** has been specifically identified for development as a **Green Hydrogen Hub** and for significant capacity expansion under the 2047 vision. ***Hence, the statement regarding V.O. Chidambaranar Port is correct.***
 
• **Paradip Port Authority** in **Odisha** is another critical major port identified for modernization to become a world-class mega port, aiming to handle **vast volumes of coal and iron ore** to support the industrial growth of Eastern India. ***Hence, the statement regarding Paradip Port is correct.***
 
• **Panaji Port**, located in **Goa**, is classified as a **minor/non-major port** and is under the jurisdiction of the **State Government (Goa Maritime Board)**. While the **MAKV 2047** covers the entire maritime ecosystem, the primary infrastructure expansion and port modernization targets for "Mega Port" status focus on the **12 Major Port Authorities** under the Union Government. Panaji Port is not among the primary Major Port Authorities identified for the **10,000 MTPA** capacity goal. ***Hence, Panaji Port is the correct option as it is NOT a Major Port Authority identified for this specific expansion.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Maritime Amrit Kaal Vision 2047 Goals:** The initiative aims to increase the total port capacity of India from the current levels to approximately **10,000 Million Tonnes Per Annum (MTPA)** by the year **2047**. It focuses on **port-led development**, reducing logistics costs, and enhancing the **Ease of Doing Business** in the maritime sector.
 
• **Development of Mega Ports:** Under this vision, India aims to develop at least **two ports** with a capacity of **1,000 MTPA** and several others with **500 MTPA** capacity. **Vizhinjam Port** in Kerala and **Vadhavan Port** in Maharashtra are also pivotal to this transshipment and mega-port strategy.
 
• **Green Port Initiative (Harit Sagar):** A significant pillar of the **MAKV 2047** is the "Harit Sagar" guidelines, which aim to achieve **Zero Carbon Emission** at Indian ports. The vision includes the installation of **renewable energy** sources, green hydrogen production, and the adoption of **LNG/Electric-powered** vessels at **Major Ports**.
 
• **Logistics and Technology:** The vision integrates the **National Logistics Portal (Marine)** and the **Sagar-Setu** mobile app to digitize maritime trade. It aims to reduce the "turnaround time" of ships to match global standards of less than **24 hours**.
 
• **Investment and Employment:** The roadmap envisions an investment of over **Rs. 80 lakh crore** in the maritime sector, which is expected to create **millions of jobs** and significantly boost India's **GDP** through increased maritime trade.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Major Ports vs. Minor Ports:** In India, there are **12 Major Ports** governed by the **Major Port Authorities Act, 2021**, and over **200 Minor/Intermediate Ports** governed by state maritime boards. The **Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways** directly oversees the Major Ports, which are the primary focus of the **Amrit Kaal Vision** for infrastructure scaling.
 
• **Maritime India Summit 2023:** This event served as the launchpad for the vision, attracting global investors and resulting in hundreds of **Memorandums of Understanding (MoUs)** worth billions of dollars to enhance **connectivity** and **maritime infrastructure**.

questions.question: Which Article authorizes the State to make special provisions for the welfare of women and children?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 15(3)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 15(3)** of the **Constitution of India** specifically empowers the **State** to make any **special provisions** for the welfare and protection of **women and children**.
 
• This clause acts as a vital exception to the general rule of non-discrimination established in **Article 15(1)** and **Article 15(2)**, which prohibits the State from discriminating against any citizen on grounds only of **religion, race, caste, sex, place of birth**, or any of them.
 
• The logic behind **Article 15(3)** is the concept of **protective discrimination** or affirmative action; it recognizes that women and children have unique social and physical positions that may require special legal safeguards.
 
• This constitutional provision has enabled the government to implement various welfare measures, such as the **reservation of seats** for women in **local self-government bodies** (Panchayats and Municipalities) and the enactment of specialized laws like the **Maternity Benefit Act**.
 
• It also provides the legal foundation for the **free education** of children and other social security schemes directed toward their growth and safety.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Article 19(5):**

 
 
• This article pertains to the **Right to Freedom** and allows the State to impose **reasonable restrictions** on the exercise of the rights to move freely and reside in any part of **India**.
 
• Such restrictions can be imposed in the interest of the **general public** or for the protection of the interests of any **Scheduled Tribe**.
 
 
 
• **Article 23(2):**
 
 
• While **Article 23(1)** prohibits **traffic in human beings** and **begar** (forced labor), **Article 23(2)** provides an exception.
 
• It permits the **State** to impose **compulsory service** for **public purposes**, such as military training or social service, provided the State does not discriminate on grounds of **religion, race, caste, or class**.
 
 
 
• **Article 16(2):**
 
 
• This article is a component of the **Right to Equality** regarding **public employment**.
 
• It mandates that no citizen shall, on grounds only of **religion, race, caste, sex, descent, place of birth, residence**, or any of them, be ineligible for, or discriminated against in respect of, any employment or office under the **State**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **Fundamental Rights** are enshrined in **Part III** of the Indian Constitution, ranging from **Article 12 to 35**.
 
• The **Right to Equality** encompasses **Articles 14 to 18**, which aim to establish social and legal equality in **India**.
 
• **Article 15(3)** was heavily cited during the formulation of the **Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education (RTE) Act, 2009**, which ensures that every child aged **6 to 14 years** has a right to formal schooling.
 
• The **Supreme Court of India** has consistently upheld that laws favoring women, such as those related to **sexual harassment at the workplace** or **domestic violence** protection, are constitutionally valid under the umbrella of **Article 15(3)**.
 
• The **73rd and 74th Constitutional Amendment Acts** of **1992**, which mandated **one-third reservation** for women in local bodies, draw their functional authority from the spirit of this article.

questions.question: The discovery of the atomic nucleus was made through which experiment?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Gold foil experiment**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The discovery of the **atomic nucleus** was the result of the **alpha-particle scattering experiment**, famously known as the **Gold foil experiment**, conducted by **Ernest Rutherford** and his team in **1911**.
 
• In this experiment, high-energy **alpha particles** (doubly charged **helium ions**) were bombarded onto a very thin sheet of **gold foil**, which was approximately **1000 atoms thick**.
 
• Rutherford observed that most of the **alpha particles** passed straight through the foil without any deflection, leading to the conclusion that most of the space inside an **atom** is **empty**.
 
• He noticed that a small fraction of the particles were deflected by small angles, and a very tiny number (about **1 in 12,000**) rebounded back, suggesting a **180-degree deflection**.
 
• Based on these observations, Rutherford concluded that the **positive charge** and nearly all the **mass** of the atom are concentrated in a very small, dense region at the center, which he named the **nucleus**. ***Hence, the statement regarding the discovery via the Gold foil experiment is correct.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Cathode Ray Experiment**:

 
 
• This experiment was conducted by **J.J. Thomson** in **1897** using a **vacuum tube**.
 
• It led to the discovery of **electrons**, the first subatomic particles to be identified.
 
• Thomson proved that **cathode rays** consisted of negatively charged particles, which he originally called "corpuscles."
 
 
 
• **Canal Ray Experiment**:
 
 
• Performed by **Eugen Goldstein** in **1886**, this experiment involved the use of a perforated cathode in a **discharge tube**.
 
• He discovered **positive rays** (canal rays) moving in the opposite direction to cathode rays.
 
• This discovery eventually led to the identification of the **proton**, which carries a **positive charge**.
 
 
 
• **Oil Drop Experiment**:
 
 
• Conducted by **Robert Millikan** and **Harvey Fletcher** in **1909** at the **University of Chicago**.
 
• The primary purpose was to measure the **elementary electronic charge**.
 
• They determined the charge of a single **electron** to be approximately **1.602 x 10^-19 Coulombs**.
 
 
 
• **Malleability of Gold**:
 
 
• **Gold** was specifically chosen for Rutherford's experiment because it is the most **malleable metal**.
 
• This property allowed the researchers to create a foil so thin that it was only a few hundred nanometers thick, ensuring that the **alpha particles** interacted with only a few layers of **atoms**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Rutherford’s Atomic Model**:

 
 
• Following the discovery, Rutherford proposed a **nuclear model** of the atom, where **electrons** revolve around the **nucleus** in circular paths called **orbits**, similar to planets revolving around the sun.
 
• He stated that the **nucleus** is extremely small; the radius of the nucleus is about **10^-15 meters**, while the radius of the **atom** is about **10^-10 meters**.
 
 
 
• **Limitations**:
 
 
• A major drawback of Rutherford's model was its inability to explain **atomic stability**. According to classical electromagnetic theory, an accelerating charged particle (the electron) should radiate energy and eventually collapse into the **nucleus**.
 
• This limitation was later addressed by **Niels Bohr** in **1913** with the introduction of **discrete energy levels** or shells.

questions.question: The Rashtrakutas were primarily known for which architectural marvel?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kailasa Temple at Ellora**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Rashtrakutas** were a powerful dynasty that ruled large parts of the **Indian subcontinent** between the **8th** and **10th centuries**.
 
• The **Kailasa Temple**, located in **Cave 16** of the **Ellora Caves** in **Sambhaji Nagar (formerly Aurangabad), Maharashtra**, is considered their greatest architectural achievement.
 
• It was commissioned by the **Rashtrakuta King Krishna I** (reigned **756–774 AD**) during the **8th century**.
 
• The temple is a **monolithic structure**, which means it was carved out of a **single massive basalt cliff**. Unlike traditional buildings that are constructed from the ground up, this temple was carved using a **top-down excavation** method.
 
• The architecture of the temple follows the **Dravidian style**, characterized by its **Gopuram** (monumental entrance tower) and complex **Vimana** (temple tower).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Rashtrakuta Dynasty:**

 
 
• The dynasty was founded by **Dantidurga** in **753 AD** after he overthrew the **Chalukyas of Badami**.
 
• Their capital was established at **Manyakheta** (modern-day **Malkhed** in **Karnataka**).
 
• Famous rulers include **Amoghavarsha I**, who was a great patron of literature and wrote the **Kavirajamarga**, the earliest available work on rhetoric, poetics, and grammar in the **Kannada language**.
 
 
 
• **Brihadeeswara Temple:**
 
 
• Located in **Thanjavur, Tamil Nadu**, this temple was built by the **Chola** emperor **Rajaraja I** in **1010 AD**.
 
• It is an outstanding example of **Chola architecture** and is dedicated to **Lord Shiva**.
 
 
 
• **Konark Sun Temple:**
 
 
• Situated in **Puri, Odisha**, this **13th-century** marvel was built by **King Narasimhadeva I** of the **Eastern Ganga Dynasty**.
 
• It is designed in the shape of a colossal **chariot** with **24 wheels** pulled by **seven horses**, dedicated to the **Sun God (Surya)**.
 
 
 
• **Sanchi Stupa:**
 
 
• Located in **Madhya Pradesh**, it is one of the oldest stone structures in India, originally commissioned by the **Mauryan Emperor Ashoka** in the **3rd century BC**.
 
• It serves as a major center for **Buddhist** pilgrimage and architecture.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **Ellora Caves** consist of **34 monasteries and temples** extending over a distance of more than **2 kilometers**. These include **17 Hindu**, **12 Buddhist**, and **5 Jain** caves, demonstrating the **religious harmony** of ancient India.
 
• The **Kailasa Temple** was designed to represent **Mount Kailash**, the celestial abode of **Lord Shiva**.
 
• The temple complex includes massive stone sculptures depicting scenes from the **Ramayana** and the **Mahabharata**, as well as a famous relief showing the demon king **Ravana** attempting to lift Mount Kailash.
 
• The **Ellora Caves** were designated as a **UNESCO World Heritage Site** in **1983** due to their cultural and historical significance.
 
• It is estimated that over **200,000 tonnes** of rock were excavated to create the **Kailasa Temple**, a feat that showcases the advanced engineering skills of the **Rashtrakuta era** artisans.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

This oversight by the **United Nations** ensures that the framework respects **international law** and the **sovereignty** of member nations.
 
• The **United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime (UNODC)** serves as the secretariat for the treaty negotiations. This body provides the necessary technical assistance and platform for all **193 member states** to negotiate terms that balance security with **human rights** and **privacy**.
 
• The process for this treaty was initiated by the **General Assembly Resolution 74/247**, which established an open-ended **Ad Hoc Committee** to elaborate a comprehensive international convention on countering the use of **information and communications technologies (ICTs)** for criminal purposes.
 
• By **October 2025**, the implementation phase and the formalization of global standards under the **United Nations** umbrella provide a unified legal basis for countries that previously lacked specific **cybersecurity** legislation.

questions.question: Which file type is most suitable for storing structured data that can be imported into spreadsheet applications?

__
 
• The **.csv** (Comma Separated Values) file format is a **plain text** file that uses a specific **delimiter** (typically a comma) to separate values, making it the most suitable format for storing **structured data**.
 
• Each line of the file corresponds to a **data record**, and each record consists of one or more **fields**, which allows it to be easily interpreted as **tabular data** by applications like **Microsoft Excel**, **Google Sheets**, and **LibreOffice Calc**.
 
• One of its primary **functions** is to facilitate the **exchange of data** between different platforms or software that might otherwise be incompatible, as it does not contain complex **formatting** or **macros**.
 
• Because it is **human-readable** and lightweight, it is widely used in **Data Science** and **software development** for exporting and importing large **databases** or **datasets**.
 
• In a **spreadsheet application**, importing a **.csv** file automatically populates the **rows** and **columns** based on the line breaks and commas present in the text file.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **.mp4 (MPEG-4 Part 14):**

 
 
• This is a **digital multimedia container** format most commonly used to store **video** and **audio** data.
 
• It can also store other data such as **subtitles** and **still images**, utilizing **lossy compression** to maintain high quality while keeping the **file size** relatively small.
 
• It is based on the **QuickTime File Format** and is widely supported across **smartphones**, **computers**, and **streaming services**.
 
 
 
• **.exe (Executable File):**
 
 
• An **.exe** file is a common **file extension** for a program that can be **executed** or run by the **Microsoft Windows** operating system.
 
• It contains **binary machine code** that the **CPU** interprets to perform specific **functions** or launch **software applications**.
 
• Unlike data files, **executable files** are not meant to be read by humans but are essential for **installing** and **running programs** on a **PC**.
 
 
 
• **.png (Portable Network Graphics):**
 
 
• This is a **raster-graphics** file format that supports **lossless data compression**.
 
• It was created as an improved, non-patented replacement for **Graphics Interchange Format (GIF)** and is the most used **lossless image** compression format on the **Internet**.
 
• Key **features** include support for **transparency** (alpha channels) and **24-bit RGB** color palettes, making it ideal for **web design** and **logos**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Data Delimiters:** While the "C" in **CSV** stands for **Comma**, some regions or **organisations** use different **delimiters** such as **semicolons** (;) or **tabs** (\t) to avoid confusion with **numerical values** that use commas as **decimal separators**.
 
• **Structure vs. Formatting:** A **CSV** file only stores the **raw data**; it cannot save **cell colors**, **font styles**, **formulas**, or **merged cells**. For these features, users must save the file in **proprietary formats** like **.xlsx**.
 
• **Historical Context:** The **CSV** format has existed since the early days of **business computing** in the **1970s**, long before the **standardisation** of **modern spreadsheet software**, proving its **longevity** and **reliability**.
 
• **Applications in Web:** Many **government agencies** and **open data portals** provide **reports** and **indices** in **CSV format** to ensure the **transparency** and **accessibility** of public data for researchers.

questions.question: According to Article 243Q, the level of municipality for a transitional area will be designated as a _________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Nagar Panchayat**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 243Q** of the **Constitution of India** mandates the constitution of three types of municipalities in every State.
 
• A **Nagar Panchayat** (by whatever name called) is constituted for a **transitional area**, which is an area in transition from a rural area to an urban area.
 
• A **Municipal Council** is constituted for a **smaller urban area**.
 
• A **Municipal Corporation** is constituted for a **larger urban area**.
 
• The **Governor** of a State, by public notification, specifies whether an area is a **transitional area**, a **smaller urban area**, or a **larger urban area** based on factors such as **population**, **density of population**, **revenue generated for local administration**, **percentage of employment in non-agricultural activities**, and **economic importance**.
 
• The **74th Amendment Act** of **1992** added **Part IX-A** to the Constitution, which deals with the administration of **Municipalities**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **74th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992**:

 
 
• This Act came into force on **June 1, 1993**.
 
• It aimed at revitalizing and strengthening **urban local bodies (ULBs)** so that they function effectively as units of self-government.
 
• It inserted the **Twelfth Schedule** into the Constitution, which contains **18 functional items** placed under the purview of municipalities.
 
 
 
• **Composition of Municipalities (Article 243R)**:
 
 
• All seats in a municipality are filled by persons chosen by **direct election** from the territorial constituencies in the municipal area.
 
• Each municipal area is divided into territorial constituencies known as **wards**.
 
 
 
• **Reservation of Seats (Article 243T)**:
 
 
• Seats are reserved for **Scheduled Castes (SC)** and **Scheduled Tribes (ST)** in every municipality in proportion to their population.
 
• Not less than **one-third (1/3)** of the total number of seats are reserved for **women** (including the number of seats reserved for SC/ST women).
 
 
 
• **Duration of Municipalities (Article 243U)**:
 
 
• The municipality has a fixed term of **5 years** from the date appointed for its first meeting.
 
• In case of dissolution, elections to constitute a new municipality must be completed within a period of **6 months**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **State Election Commission (Article 243ZA)**:

 
 
• The **superintendence**, **direction**, and **control** of the preparation of electoral rolls and the conduct of all elections to the municipalities are vested in the **State Election Commission**.
 
 
 
• **State Finance Commission (Article 243Y)**:
 
 
• The Finance Commission constituted under **Article 243-I** (for Panchayats) also reviews the financial position of the municipalities and makes recommendations to the **Governor** regarding the distribution of **taxes**, **duties**, **tolls**, and **fees** between the State and the Municipalities.
 
 
 
• **District Planning Committee (Article 243ZD)**:
 
 
• Every State must constitute a **District Planning Committee** at the district level to consolidate the plans prepared by the **Panchayats** and the **Municipalities** in the district.
 
 
 
• **Metropolitan Planning Committee (Article 243ZE)**:
 
 
• In every **metropolitan area** (an area having a population of **10 lakh** or more), a Metropolitan Planning Committee must be constituted to prepare a draft development plan for the metropolitan area as a whole.

⇒ 16 + 3 − 8

⇒ 19 − 8 = 11

BODMAS Rule

Order of operations: Brackets → Orders → Division → Multiplication → Addition → Subtraction.

Division and Multiplication Priority

Division and multiplication have equal priority and are solved left to right.

Addition and Subtraction Rule

After ÷ and ×, perform + and − from left to right.

Common Mistake

Solving left to right directly without applying BODMAS leads to wrong answers.

questions.question: Ashoka was the viceroy of which region under his father Bindusara’s reign?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ujjain**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ashoka**, one of the greatest emperors of ancient India, served as the **Viceroy (Governor)** of **Ujjain** (the capital of the **Avanti** province) during the reign of his father, **Bindusara**.
 
• As a prince, he was also sent to **Taxila** (Takshashila) to suppress a major revolt against the central **Mauryan** administration, where he demonstrated exceptional military and diplomatic skills. ***Hence, the statement regarding his viceroyship in Ujjain is correct.***
 
• **Ujjain** was a highly strategic and commercial hub in central India, connecting the trade routes between the **Gangetic Valley** and the western coast, making it a crucial administrative post for a royal prince.
 
• His tenure in **Ujjain** is historically significant because it was there that he reportedly met **Devi**, the daughter of a trader from **Vidisha**, who later became his wife and gave birth to his children, **Mahinda** and **Sanghamitta**.
 
• The experience gained by **Ashoka** while governing provinces like **Ujjain** and **Taxila** prepared him for the complex administrative challenges he would face after ascending the throne in **268 BCE**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Bindusara (r. 297 – 273 BCE):**

 
 
• He was the son of **Chandragupta Maurya** and the second ruler of the **Mauryan Dynasty**.
 
• Known by the title **Amitraghata** (Slayer of Foes), he maintained the vast empire inherited from his father and kept friendly relations with **Hellenic** kingdoms.
 
 
 
• **Patliputra:**
 
 
• Located near modern-day **Patna**, it served as the imperial capital of the **Mauryan Empire**.
 
• While **Bindusara** ruled the empire from this central seat of power, his sons were appointed as **Kumaramatyas** (Princely Viceroys) in distant provinces.
 
 
 
• **Tosali:**
 
 
• It was the provincial capital of the **Kalinga** region.
 
• This region only became a formal part of the **Mauryan Empire** after **Ashoka** conquered it in the **Kalinga War** around **261 BCE**, which took place years after his father's death.
 
 
 
• **Saurashtra:**
 
 
• This western region (modern **Gujarat**) was managed by local governors such as **Pushyagupta** under **Chandragupta Maurya** and **Tushaspa** (a Yavana/Greek) under **Ashoka**.
 
• It was famous for the construction of the **Sudarsana Lake**, an important irrigation project of that era.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Succession Struggle:** After the death of **Bindusara** in **273 BCE**, a war of succession broke out between **Ashoka** and his brothers (notably **Susima**). According to Buddhist traditions like the **Mahavamsa**, **Ashoka** emerged victorious and was formally crowned in **268 BCE**.
 
• **Mauryan Administrative Divisions:** The empire was divided into four main provinces: **Uttarapatha** (Taxila), **Avantiratha** (Ujjain), **Dakshinapatha** (Suvarnagiri), and **Prachyapatha** (Tosali, after the Kalinga conquest).
 
• **Inscriptions and Sources:** Much of what we know about **Ashoka's** early life and administration comes from the **Edits of Ashoka**, the **Ashokavadana**, and **Dipavamsa**. These texts highlight his transition from **Chanda Ashoka** (Fierce Ashoka) to **Dharma Ashoka** (Pious Ashoka).
 
• **Geographical Extent:** Under **Bindusara**, the empire spanned almost the entire Indian subcontinent, excluding the far south (Tamil regions) and **Kalinga** on the eastern coast.

questions.question: The FAO Food Price Index (FFPI), which monitors monthly fluctuations in the global prices of a basket of internationally traded food commodities, averaged how many points in December 2025?

• The **base period** for the FFPI is currently **2014-2016**, where the index value is set to **100**. Any value above 100 indicates an increase in prices relative to that base period. ***Hence, the mention of 124.3 points represents a 24.3% increase over the base.***
 
• The FFPI serves as a crucial indicator for **global food security** and **inflationary trends**. It helps the **United Nations** and various **governments** monitor food price volatility, which can impact **low-income countries** and **vulnerable populations**.
 
• Monthly fluctuations in the index are often driven by factors such as **weather patterns**, **geopolitical conflicts**, changes in **energy costs** (which affect production and transport), and **currency exchange rates**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Vegetable Oil Price Index:** It monitors the international prices of **palm oil**, **soy oil**, **sunflower oil**, and **rapeseed oil**.
 
• **Dairy Price Index:** This includes the prices of **butter**, **whole milk powder (WMP)**, **skim milk powder (SMP)**, and **cheese**.
 
• **Meat Price Index:** It covers the prices of **poultry**, **bovine** (beef), **pig**, and **ovine** (lamb) meat.
 
• **Sugar Price Index:** This tracks the **International Sugar Agreement** prices and reflects global sugar trade dynamics.
 
 
 
• **Organization Profile:**
 
 
• The **Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO)** is a specialized agency of the **United Nations** that leads international efforts to defeat hunger.
 
• It was founded on **16 October 1945**, a date now celebrated annually as **World Food Day**.
 
• The headquarters of the FAO is located in **Rome, Italy**.
 
• As of **2024**, the organization has **194 Member Nations**, two associate members, and one member organization, the **European Union**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Historical Context:** The FFPI was first introduced by the FAO in **1996** as a public good to help monitor developments in the global agricultural commodity markets.
 
• **Economic Impact:** High food prices or extreme **volatility** can lead to **social unrest** and economic instability, particularly in **import-dependent** nations. For instance, the spikes in **2008** and **2011** led to significant global food crises.
 
• **Data Collection:** The FAO collects price data from various **international markets** and **trading hubs** to ensure the index remains a reliable and **unbiased** representation of the global market.
 
• **Reports:** The FAO releases the **Food Outlook** report twice a year (usually in **June** and **November**), providing a detailed analysis of market trends and forecasts for major food groups.

questions.question: In which year was Tamil given the status of classical language by the Constitution of India?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Tamil** was the first language in **India** to be officially accorded the status of a **Classical Language**.
 
• The announcement was made by the **Government of India** in **October 2004** following a long-standing demand from scholars and the state government.
 
• To be categorized as a **Classical Language**, the language must possess high antiquity of its early texts/recorded history over a period of **1500–2000 years**.
 
• The criteria also specify that the **literary tradition** must be original and not borrowed from another speech community, which **Tamil** fulfills through its **Sangam literature**.
 
• The recognition was formalized through a notification by the **Ministry of Home Affairs** on **October 12, 2004**, marking a significant milestone for **Dravidian languages**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• Following **Tamil**, several other languages have been granted **Classical status** based on their historical and literary significance:

 
 
• **Sanskrit** was declared a classical language in **2005**.
 
• Both **Telugu** and **Kannada** were granted the status in **2008**.
 
• **Malayalam** was added to the list in **2013**.
 
• **Odia** became the sixth language to receive the honor in **2014**.
 
 
 
• In a historic decision in **October 2024**, the **Union Cabinet**, chaired by **Prime Minister Narendra Modi**, approved the inclusion of five more languages: **Marathi**, **Pali**, **Prakrit**, **Assamese**, and **Bengali**.
 
• The **Ministry of Education** provides various benefits for these languages, including two major **International Awards** for eminent scholars and the establishment of a **Centre of Excellence for Studies in Classical Languages**.

• **Tamil** is part of the **Dravidian language family** and is one of the longest-surviving classical languages in the world, with recorded history spanning over **2,000 years**.
 
• Apart from **India**, **Tamil** holds official status in **Sri Lanka** and **Singapore**, and it is widely spoken in the **Indian State** of **Tamil Nadu** and the **Union Territory** of **Puducherry**.
 
• The **Sangam period** (approximately **300 BCE to 300 CE**) produced a vast body of **Tamil** literature, including the famous **Tolkappiyam** (grammar) and **Eight Anthologies (Ettuthokai)**, which served as a primary basis for its classical claim.

questions.question: Which aspect of Hindu religion is reflected through the Raut Nacha dance form in Chhattisgarh ?

__
 
• **Raut Nacha** is a traditional folk dance performed by the **Yadav/Yadu** (also known as **Raut**) community in the state of **Chhattisgarh**, India.
 
• This dance form is deeply rooted in the **devotion** to **Lord Krishna** and reflects the **warrior** spirit and cultural heritage of the cowherd community, who consider themselves **descendants** of the **Yaduvanshi** lineage.
 
• The performance is a symbolic representation of the **victory** of **good over evil**, specifically commemorating the **battle** between **Lord Krishna** and the demon king **Kansa**. ***Hence, the option "Memories of Lord Krishna" is correct.***
 
• The dance is traditionally performed during the **period** following **Diwali**, specifically on the **auspicious** day of **Dev Uthani Ekadashi** (the 11th day of the **Shukla Paksha** in the month of **Kartik**), which is believed to be the time when the gods awaken from their sleep.
 
• Performers wear **colorful**, vibrant costumes and carry **decorated sticks** or **shields**, performing **synchronized** steps and **rhythmic** movements to the beat of traditional instruments like the **Mandhar** (drum).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Significance of Dohas:** A unique feature of the dance is the **recitation** of **Dohas** (rhyming couplets). These couplets often contain **philosophical** meanings, **moral** lessons, or **praises** of **Lord Krishna** and the **ancestors**.

• **Legends of Lord Shiva:** While **Chhattisgarh** has many **Shaivite** traditions, **Raut Nacha** is strictly a **Vaishnavite** (Krishna-centric) folk form. ***Hence, this statement is incorrect.***
 
 
 
• **Traditional Instruments:** The dance is accompanied by the **Dhol**, **Nagada**, **Singi** (trumpet), and **flutes**, creating a **high-energy** atmosphere.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Cultural Identity:** The dance serves as a **social gathering** tool for the **Raut** community to strengthen **communal bonds** and pass down **ancestral** stories to the **younger generation**.

questions.question: Which pair of keyboard shortcuts is used to quickly copy and paste text?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ctrl + C and Ctrl + V**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ctrl + C and Ctrl + V**: This pair represents the standard keyboard shortcuts in almost all **Graphical User Interfaces (GUIs)** for performing the copy and paste operations. **Ctrl + C** is used to duplicate the selected data to the **Clipboard**, while **Ctrl + V** is used to insert that data into a specific location. *Hence, this option is correct.*
 
• **Function of Copy (Ctrl + C)**: When a user selects a piece of text, image, or file and presses **Ctrl + C**, the computer stores a reference or the actual data in a temporary storage area known as the **Clipboard**. This allows the original content to remain in its place while creating a replica.
 
• **Function of Paste (Ctrl + V)**: The paste command retrieves whatever is currently stored in the **system clipboard** and places it at the **cursor's location**. This function can be used multiple times to create several copies of the same item until a new item is copied.
 
• **Origin**: These commands were popularized by **Larry Tesler** while working at **Xerox PARC** in the **1970s**. They became industry standards with the rise of **Apple Macintosh** and **Microsoft Windows** operating systems.
 
• **Efficiency**: Using these **keyboard shortcuts** significantly increases **productivity** compared to using a mouse to navigate through "Edit" menus or right-click context menus.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Ctrl + F and Ctrl + C**: In this pair, **Ctrl + F** is the shortcut for **Find**, which opens a search box to locate specific text within a document or webpage. **Ctrl + C** is for **Copy**. While both are useful, they do not function together as a "copy-paste" pair. *Hence, this option is incorrect.*
 
• **Ctrl + Tab and Ctrl + S**: **Ctrl + Tab** is a **navigation shortcut** used to switch between open tabs in web browsers like **Google Chrome** or **Mozilla Firefox**. **Ctrl + S** is the **Save** command, used to commit changes to a file on the **hard drive**. *Hence, this option is incorrect.*
 
• **Ctrl + F and Ctrl + S**: This combination links the **Find** utility and the **Save** command. It is often used during editing but does not involve duplicating or moving text. *Hence, this option is incorrect.*
 
• **Clipboard Management**: Modern versions of **Windows 10** and **Windows 11** have introduced **Windows + V**, which allows users to view their **Clipboard History**, enabling them to choose from several previously copied items rather than just the most recent one.
 
• **Cut Command (Ctrl + X)**: Often confused with copy, **Ctrl + X** removes the selected text from its original position and places it on the **Clipboard**. This is used for "moving" text rather than "duplicating" it.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Universal Compatibility**: These shortcuts work across various platforms, including **Microsoft Word**, **Excel**, **PowerPoint**, and most **web browsers**.
 
• **macOS Variants**: On **Apple** computers, the **Command (⌘)** key is used instead of **Control**. Therefore, Copy is **Command + C** and Paste is **Command + V**.
 
• **Undo and Redo**: To complement copy-paste, users frequently use **Ctrl + Z** for **Undo** (reversing an action) and **Ctrl + Y** (or **Ctrl + Shift + Z**) for **Redo**.
 
• **Select All**: Before copying large amounts of text, users often use **Ctrl + A** to **Select All** content within a window or text box.

questions.question: Which volcano type is also known as a stratovolcano due to its layered structure?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Composite volcano**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **Composite volcano**, also known as a **stratovolcano**, is a tall, conical volcano built up by many **layers** (strata) of hardened **lava**, **tephra**, **pumice**, and **volcanic ash**.
 
• These volcanoes are characterized by a **steep profile** and periodic **explosive eruptions** and **effusive eruptions**, although some have exhibited collapsed craters called **calderas**.
 
• The **magma** forming this type of volcano is typically **intermediate to high in silica** content (andesitic, dacitic, or rhyolitic), which makes it more **viscous** (thick) than the basaltic magma found in shield volcanoes.
 
• Due to high **viscosity**, the lava travels short distances from the vent before cooling and hardening, which contributes to the **conical shape** and steep slopes of the **stratovolcano**.
 
• Famous examples of **composite volcanoes** include **Mount Fuji** in **Japan**, **Mount Rainier** and **Mount St. Helens** in the **United States**, and **Mount Vesuvius** in **Italy**.
 
• These volcanoes are most commonly found along **subduction zones**, where one tectonic plate is being pushed beneath another, such as along the **Pacific Ring of Fire**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Shield Volcano:**

 
 
• A **Shield volcano** is a type of volcano usually built almost entirely of **fluid basaltic lava flows**.
 
• They are named for their **large size** and **low profile**, resembling a warrior's shield lying on the ground.
 
• The **low viscosity** of the lava allows it to flow over **great distances**, creating broad, gentle slopes.
 
• The **Hawaiian Islands** are composed of a chain of shield volcanoes, including **Mauna Loa** and **Kilauea**.
 
 
 
• **Cinder Cone Volcano:**
 
 
• **Cinder cones** are the simplest type of volcano, built from **particles and blobs of congealed lava** ejected from a single vent.
 
• As the gas-charged lava is blown violently into the air, it breaks into small fragments that solidify and fall as **cinders** (tephra) around the vent to form a **circular or oval cone**.
 
• Most cinder cones have a **bowl-shaped crater** at the summit and rarely rise more than **a thousand feet** above their surroundings.
 
• An example is **Parícutin** in **Mexico**, which grew out of a cornfield in **1943**.
 
 
 
• **Fissure Volcano:**
 
 
• A **Fissure volcano** or **vent** is a linear volcanic vent through which lava erupts, usually **without any explosive activity**.
 
• The vent is usually **a few meters wide** but may be **many kilometers long**.
 
• Fissure vents can cause **large flood basalts** and are common in **Iceland** and along **mid-ocean ridges**.

• **Ring of Fire:** A **40,000 km** horseshoe-shaped basin in the **Pacific Ocean** where a large number of **earthquakes** and **volcanic eruptions** occur. It contains approximately **75%** of the world's active volcanoes.
 
• **Pyroclastic Flow:** A fast-moving current of **hot gas and volcanic matter** (collectively known as tephra) that moves away from a volcano reaching speeds of up to **700 km/h**. This is a common and deadly feature of **composite volcano** eruptions.
 
• **Magma vs. Lava:** **Magma** is the molten rock stored **underground**, while **Lava** is the term for magma once it **reaches the surface** through a volcanic vent.
 
• **Volcanic Explosivity Index (VEI):** A relative measure of the **explosiveness of volcanic eruptions**, ranging from **0 to 8**. **Stratovolcanoes** typically score higher on this index compared to shield volcanoes.

questions.question: Three positive integers a, b, and c satisfy: gcd(a, b)=12, gcd(b, c)=18, gcd(c, a)=6. If a+b+c=6k for some positive integer k, then the minimum possible value of k is:

Take minimum structure using primes:

12 = 2² × 3, 18 = 2 × 3², 6 = 2 × 3

Assign: a = 2²×3, b = 2²×3², c = 2×3²

⇒ a = 12, b = 36, c = 18

⇒ Sum = 66 = 6k ⇒ k = 11

**∴ Answer = 11**

**Minimum values:**

⇒ a = 12, b = 36, c = 18

**Calculations:**

⇒ Sum = 12 + 36 + 18 = 66

⇒ 66 = 6k ⇒ k = 11

**Final Answer:** 11

questions.question: In which year was the Padhe Bharat Badhe Bharat (PBBB) scheme launched?
questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Padhe Bharat Badhe Bharat (PBBB)** scheme was officially launched in **2014** as a nationwide sub-programme of the **Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan (SSA)**.
 
• The primary objective of the scheme is to improve the **reading**, **writing**, and **mathematical skills** of children in **Class I** and **Class II**.
 
• It was introduced by the **Ministry of Human Resource Development** (now known as the **Ministry of Education**) to ensure that every child attains foundational literacy and numeracy.
 
• The program recognizes that the first few years of **primary education** are critical for a child's future learning outcomes and focuses on building a strong foundation in **language** and **arithmetic**.
 
• The scheme provides a framework for **States** and **Union Territories** to implement effective classroom practices and teacher training modules specifically designed for early graders.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Twin Tracks of PBBB:**

 
 
• The scheme operates on two main tracks: **Early Reading and Writing with Comprehension (ERWC)** and **Early Mathematics (EM)**.
 
• **ERWC** focuses on enabling children to read with understanding and express themselves in writing.
 
• **EM** is designed to help children understand **reasoning**, **numbers**, **shapes**, and **measurement** through activity-based learning.
 
 
 
• **Integration with Samagra Shiksha:**
 
 
• Following the reorganization of educational schemes, **Padhe Bharat Badhe Bharat** has been subsumed under the **Samagra Shiksha Abhiyan**, which is an integrated scheme for school education from **Pre-school** to **Class XII**.
 
• This integration ensures a seamless transition and continuous monitoring of learning levels across all stages of school education in **India**.
 
 
 
• **Related Initiatives:**
 
 
• In **2021**, the government launched the **NIPUN Bharat Mission** (National Initiative for Proficiency in Reading with Understanding and Numeracy).
 
• **NIPUN Bharat** aims to achieve the goal of **universal foundational literacy and numeracy** for every child by the end of **Grade 3** by the year **2026-27**.
 
• These missions align with the goals of the **National Education Policy (NEP) 2020**, which prioritizes **foundational learning**.
 
 
 
• **Target Beneficiaries and Impact:**
 
 
• The scheme targets children in the **age group** of **6 to 8 years** studying in government and government-aided schools across the **country**.
 
• It emphasizes the use of **pedagogical tools** and **print-rich environments** in schools to make learning more engaging and effective for young learners.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The scheme encourages the use of **Mother Tongue** or **Home Language** as the medium of instruction in early years to bridge the gap between home and school environments.
 
• Monitoring of the scheme is done through the **Project Approval Board (PAB)** of the **Ministry of Education**, which reviews the progress made by different **States** annually.
 
• Special focus is given to **District-level** implementation and the creation of **Teacher Resource Material** to help educators handle multi-grade and multi-level classrooms efficiently.
